subject: flamingo
pitch: An elegant flamingo standing tall in shallow water. Candy-pink feathers deepening to coral on the wings, with a flash of black flight feathers at the wing tips, an S-curved neck, a bent beak that is pale pink with a black tip, pale yellow eyes and long rose-coloured legs with knobbly knees and webbed feet.
reasoning:
I'm sketching the flamingo's proportions — standing roughly 1.4 meters tall with legs about 0.85 meters, two legs in a resting pose, and a thin shallow water disc at the base so everything stays grounded with nothing floating above the ground plane.

Now I'm planning the skeleton: a hips root joint anchoring spine, neck, and tail chains, with the body built as a sweep along a curved spine path and an S-curved neck leading up to the head. I'm working out joint coordinates for the leg chains too, adjusting the overall scale down to a more realistic flamingo height around 1.2–1.5 meters with the hips lower and thighs short and feathered near the body.

Now I'm sizing the lower leg segments so the tibiotarsus and tarsus lengths sum close to the hip-to-ground distance, keeping the leg nearly straight with a slight backward bend at the ankle joint like a real flamingo's visible knee. I'm setting up a three-joint leg chain from hip to knee to ankle, then planning three webbed forward-facing toes extending from the ankle tip with membrane between them.

For the webbed foot I'm extruding a flat triangular outline oriented so it lies on the ground plane, with toe rods along the edges and thin webbing between them, plus small knobby spheres at the knee joints for detail.

I also need to work out the water layer height carefully so the feet aren't hidden beneath it -- placing the water disc with ripple rings just below the feet so the legs appear to be standing in shallow water rather than submerged.

For the body, I'm picking colors: candy pink for the torso and coral for the wings, then shaping each folded wing as a teardrop extrusion along the side of the body with layered coverts, secondaries, and dark primary tips for a feathered look.

Designing layered feather extrusions...

Still laying out feather rows...

I'll use a sharp tip for primaries but rounder for coverts. For coloring, I'm thinking of applying a countershaded gradient to the body — deeper pink on the back, lighter on the belly — while keeping the neck a flat pink and limiting the total palette. Now I'm working out the body's spine sweep with a radius profile from tail to chest.

Still writing the body shape function...

Mapping out the neck curve as an S-shape rising to roughly 1.5m, tapering from 0.04 to 0.032 radius, with seven joints forming six spans parented to the spine's last joint. I'm also setting up the spine chain with four points and starting to define the tail chain root.

Planning tail feathers as a fan of five thin extrusions angled slightly outward, around 0.25 length and parented to the tail joint.

Now I'm setting up wing rigging: adding shoulder, wrist, and wingtip joints on each side parented to the spine, forming a chain with a "wing" role so feathers can later attach along it.

For feather bones, I'm assigning primaries to the wrist joint and coverts to the shoulder joint, treating the joint names as the bone attachment references. Then I'm planning the head joint at the end of the neck chain, parented to the last neck joint and aimed appropriately.

Now I'm working out the head geometry—a slightly elongated sphere scaled anisotropically—and sketching the flamingo beak as a bent bezier curve from the head front, with the upper bill sweeping forward before curving downward partway along its length.

Still working out the beak geometry...

Placing the pupil smaller and slightly offset outward, and deciding to skip extra eyelid detailing for simplicity. For the bill coloring, I'm setting up a pale pink base transitioning to black on the distal half, matching real flamingo coloration patterns.

Now I'm defining the neck's mottled pink surface, tapering the neck radius from thicker at the base to narrower near the head, with rounded caps connecting chest to neck. Then I'm setting up the leg sweeps along a three-bone chain.

Setting up the leg bone chains with hip, knee, and ankle joints parented to the hips, tapering the limb radius along the chain, and defining the ankle tip position for the foot/toes attachment.

Still computing foot geometry...

Now I'm laying out the water disc touching the floor plane, then adding small triangular ripple ring shapes around each foot using lathe geometry, colored pale cyan-white to contrast against the water.

I should bind the ripple rings to the hips bone so they stay fixed near ground level rather than tracking the legs, then confirm the water radius comfortably fits under the model's full height. Now I'm starting a helper function for extruded plate shapes with configurable outline, position, direction, thickness, color, and bone binding.

I'm deciding whether to apply a bevel for nicer shading, but to avoid edge-crossing errors with the small feather angles I'll skip it and just taper the thickness instead. Writing the feather outline shape...

Now I'm working out the wing feather function parameters and checking that the cross product of direction vectors correctly gives the thickness axis along X, confirming no mirroring is needed since the outline is symmetric.

Next I'm laying out the side-view geometry for the wing rows, figuring out where the body's curved profile intersects the wing plane at different heights so the coverts shingle naturally against the flank.

Still working out the feather offset math...

I'm deciding that the narrowing body letting the wing float outward actually looks like a natural folded wing, so I'll leave it as-is. Now I'm picking coverts and feather row colors—shifting from pink-coral at the shoulder to deeper coral through the mid feathers, dark near-black for primaries, and a softer pink-coral for secondaries—before setting up the row parameters starting with seven primaries.

Adjusting primary feather placement and lengths...

Still tuning coverts...

For the wing bones I'll attach feather parts to the joint chain using the wrist and shoulder joints directly. I'm skipping extra chest ruffles and spots, keeping the breast simple with lighter pink. For the tail, I'm setting up a short joint chain off the spine with two tail segments and will attach tail feathers to that.

Now I'm computing the fan of tail feathers—five plates positioned at the base of the tail bone, with directions spread across a roughly 48-degree arc, using perpendicular vectors to orient each feather's width and thickness correctly, with slight vertical layering between them.

For the head, I'm adding details like the crown, eye, beak edge lines, and fleshy bill base, plus a dark rim behind each eye using a small flat black cylinder disc.

I'm deciding to skip extra neck feather texturing like ruffles or stripes to keep things simple, and instead focusing on positioning the head joint at the end of the neck, orienting it forward-level to align with the bill.

For the head itself, I'm shaping a sphere with scale [0.85, 0.9, 1.25] to stretch it slightly wider and longer without adding rotation axes, keeping orientation in world space. Then I'm placing the eyes symmetrically off the head's local position using a sign factor for left/right sides.

Now I'm working out the bill geometry, planning a curved path from a start point buried inside the head front through several control points that taper outward and downward, with decreasing radii along the length for a natural beak shape.

Now I'm setting up the neck as a swept chain with a tapering radius joining the chest, considering whether to add a blending ball or fluff sphere at the junction, and sketching the body sweep along the spine with its own radius and paint color.

I'm working out the spine and neck joint chains: the spine runs from hips through a few catmull points to a neck base, and the neck's first point must match the spine's endpoint so they connect smoothly, with proper parent-child joint relationships.

Now I'm shaping the neck curve into an S-bend—bulging forward near the bottom, pulling back in the middle, then curving forward again toward the top where the head sits, with the beak angled downward. I'm also setting up the leg structure, starting with hip positions mirrored for left and right sides.

Setting up IK limb geometry...

Defining the leg chain with hip, knee, and ankle joints, parented to the hips with a rose-colored sweep, then adding small icosahedron knobs at the knee joint for extra detail.

For the feet, I'm building a toe chain per leg with three angled toes branching off the foot tip, computing their directions and segment lengths to place base, mid, and tip points.

Still writing toe geometry...

For the web between toes, I'm extruding a thin membrane using the appropriate axis orientation so the thickness lines up correctly with the leg plane.

I'm setting eye colors — yellow iris with a dark pupil — and planning the coat shading by composing a countershade effect over a mottled pink pattern, pulling in the limb and paint helper imports I'll need for the skin texture.

Now I'm building the wing chains for each side as a three-joint sequence from shoulder to wrist to wingtip, parented to one of the spine joints, making sure the joint positions stay within the body.

Writing feather extrusion helper...

Simplifying the thickness to a constant value, then designing a row generator function that defines feather parameters like position, count, angle range, length, and width so I can build out the primary feathers with varying tip positions.

Working through tail feathers, eyes with small spherical pupils positioned locally near the face, and the water lathe geometry attached to the hips bone. I'm also setting up foot positions and ripple rings using a closed triangular outline rotated around each foot location.
